summary.intent: Revert a prior 'nothing-to-release' JSON-field commit and instead split the inference trait so disabled inference (NoInference) skips inference-only preparation without changing the meaning of requires_full_history().
summary.outcome: Reverted 4e4b8a178 as signed commit 13a4ab2ef, added an is_active() trait method gating inference prep in aggregate.rs, and added four passing unit tests with negative controls. The full gate (pre-push, lint, doc-check, test, fuzz-check) exited 0 and just bench showed constant git process counts across 50/200/500 packages; the trait split was committed signed locally, not pushed.

repo: Work is gated by a `just` full gate (pre-push, lint, doc-check, test, fuzz-check) and a `just bench` recipe that reports git process counts, which must stay constant as package count grows.
Commits are signed, verified via signature status 'G'.
There is a review checklist; item 11 requires tracing consumers of changed trait behaviour.
Review is done with `codex review --base origin/main` in rounds after the local commit.

Tests use a recording git runner that can inject failures, a configurable inference adapter, and real repos (including a `--depth 1` shallow clone) created via helpers like init_repo and TagIndex::commit_of.

code.finding: Inference trait now has is_active() (default true) alongside requires_full_history(); NoInference returns false for both.
is_active() gates resolve_since, pathspecs/policy inputs, window spec and the infer call; the full-history/shallow check still uses requires_full_history().
The only production consumer of NoInference (the pending hint), so the trait split changes no other behaviour.

workflow: Negative controls (removing each gate and confirming the matching test fails) validate that new tests actually exercise the guarded behaviour.
Running the gate in the background with recorded exit codes lets other work (reading checklists, tracing consumers) proceed in parallel.
The sandbox blocked writes to a worktree's git dir not created by the session, so git writes had to be retried unsandboxed.

friction: Sandbox blocked git writes to the worktree's git dir, requiring unsandboxed retries for the signed revert and commit.
open_items: Run `codex review --base origin/main` rounds on the committed change.
